analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | CPI | HVAC changes | pickup analysis 14 Oct 2026
key_insights: US S&P futures up modestly led by technology after ASML raised its outlook and is looking for ways to produce more chip-making machines to meet demand. KOSPI -44bps, Japan flat, Europe broadly stronger with France +70bps.
Crude up 100bps with Brent $106 and WTI $95 after a flare-up in Middle East attacks. IEA warns diesel will remain constrained well into 2027.
10-year yield continues a modest grind lower at 5.19%, DXY steady at $102, Bitcoin down slightly to $83k.

GS expects September core CPI +0.24% m/m (consensus +0.2%), +2.46% y/y (consensus +2.5%), and headline +0.59% (consensus +0.6%), driven by higher energy prices. This is consistent with a 0.20% core PCE increase in September.

Component expectations for September CPI: autos inflation picks up (used cars +0.5%, new cars +0.2%, auto insurance +0.2%), shelter stays benign (OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%), airfares +3.0% on higher jet fuel.

GS expects core CPI of about 0.2% in October, with upward pressure from seasonal-factor distortions caused by missing data from last year's government shutdown, and about 0.1% in November and December on slowing shelter and shrinking tariff contributions.
China September CPI +0.9% y/y (August +0.8%) on energy and transportation services. PPI +5.0% y/y (August +3.8%) on energy goods and chemicals.

GS raised its China 2026/27 PPI forecasts to 2.8%/0.3% (from 2.0%/0.0%) and lowered its CPI forecasts to 0.8%/0.6% (from 1.0%/1.0%) on weak domestic demand and fading energy boost in 2027. Y/y PPI likely turns negative as early as Q2 2027 on a high base.
China September exports +36.3% y/y and imports +31.0% y/y, well above consensus. Trade surplus widened to US$133.5bn (NSA) from US$119.1bn in August, the largest monthly surplus on record.

AZZ fiscal Q2 beat: EPS $2.00 vs $1.86 expected, revenue $487mm vs $463mm, EBITDA $111mm vs $104mm. Metal Coatings +23%, Precoat Metals +12%. FY Feb 2027 guidance raised to EPS $7-7.30 (prior $6.75-7.15), revenue $1.825-1.875bn, EBITDA $380-420mm. Implied move 5%.

SAIC named Ken Crews (previously NOC CFO) as EVP and CFO elect, joining end of October and assuming the role in early December. Desk calls the move somewhat surprising, from a $70bn market cap company to a $6bn one.
RTX was awarded a maximum $8bn USAF contract.

GS (Joe) upgraded TT to Buy and downgraded LII and CARR to Neutral. Applied HVAC (JCI, TT) has outperformed Resi HVAC (LII, CARR) over the past year (JCI +47%, LII -33%), and GS expects this to continue over 12 months.

GS FY27 estimates vs consensus: JCI +6%, TT +4%, LII -4%, CARR -3%. Resi HVAC faces more competition and weaker pricing, with tepid demand on low housing turnover and affordability. Applied HVAC backlog is up about 50% on average this year for JCI and TT as longer-cycle AI/data-center power generation parts are booking orders beyond 2030.

GS (Mark Delaney) on pickups: OEMs typically see 2-3 years of better sales after a truck refresh, full-size pickups are a growing share of the US auto market and likely drive a significant portion of F and GM EBIT. GM's MY27 Sierra/Silverado refresh launches later in 2026.

GM has said truck volumes from the back half of 2027 to the end of 2027 could be flattish while new variants ramp, with the refresh more material to sales in 2028. Net pricing gains may be limited because pricing on the current generation has stayed strong.

Desk is watching automation names with positive checks, and auto parts retail checks that are more mixed. Early bogeys include PCAR TP&O gross margins, NVT orders, MMM organic growth, and EMR, ROK, JCI, WWD guides.

tension_points.bull_case: Applied HVAC (JCI, TT) has outperformed, with GS FY27 estimates above consensus (JCI +6%, TT +4%) and backlog up about 50% on average this year from AI/data-center orders booking beyond 2030.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Resi HVAC pricing and demand holding up better than GS expects, which would remove the estimate gap versus consensus.
